It does not check that the caller passes that file as the `--module` mounted at `/gate/prepush_affected_tests.py` (scripts/prepush_test_gate_run.sh line 251).
  WHY: The filename already appears in comments and other lines of scripts/heal_reproduce.sh, scripts/implement_step_prepush_test_gate.sh and scripts/review_autofix_step_prepush_test_gate.sh, so the `test_scanned_host_file_matches_the_registry` assertion always passes for this entry. If a caller switches to a different module, tests-sandbox-python stays green while testing a file that is no longer the one mounted. All five reviewers rated this NIT.

- tests/test_sandbox_python_coverage.py:resolve_host_basenames(), caller loop `resolved = value if value in text else None` (kind == "names"); also kind == "variable" `if f'"${{{value}}}"' in text` | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The "names" check only asks whether `prepush_affected_tests.py` appears anywhere in the caller and then returns the table's own literal. It passes for every caller: scripts/heal_reproduce.sh lines 123 and 416-419, scripts/implement_step_prepush_test_gate.sh lines 260 and 268-270, scripts/review_autofix_step_prepush_test_gate.sh lines 316-321. The "variable" branch only checks that `"${guard_hook}"` appears somewhere in scripts/ai_engine.sh; today it is the value passed on line 562.
  WHY: If a caller changes the module it passes to scripts/prepush_test_gate_run.sh (mounted on line 251) but the old filename stays in a comment, the guard stays green. tests-sandbox-python then tests a file that is not the one mounted. Suggested fix: use a structural regex such as `re.search(r'(?:module=|install\b[^\n]*")[^"\n]*' + re.escape(value), text)`.
- HARDENING: tests/test_sandbox_python_coverage.py resolve_host_basenames() "names" `else:` branch: replace `value in text` with the regex above and keep the existing failure reason. Estimated 2-3 lines; HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
